requirement_text.REQ-209: Fifth requirement of S7. Ports what's portable from tests/differential/ (tests/differential/corpus/conditions_v1.json, confirmed 15 entries this session by counting condition_id fields; tests/differential/differential_test.zig, 476+ lines). WHY THIS IS A REGRESSION PORT, NOT A DIFFERENTIAL PORT (stated explicitly because the stage doc's own scope line names "tests/differential/" without qualifying this distinction, and a future reader could otherwise assume a second Elixir condition evaluator needs building to diff against). R-Co's differential_test.zig evaluates each corpus condition_text with BOTH vendor/cel (a vendored CEL library) and src/expr (R-Co's own hand-written replacement), asserting they agree -- this was R-Co's own EXP-102 cutover gate, retiring CEL entirely once green (confirmed by reading the file's own header comment and lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex's moduledoc this session: "R-Co's EXP-102 cut over *from* a vendored CEL... *to* src/expr, retiring CEL entirely"). Letflow never had two implementations -- lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex (REQ-050, extended by REQ-197/REQ-198) is a direct Elixir port of R-Co's POST-cutover src/expr grammar only; Letflow has no vendored-CEL equivalent and is not building one. So this requirement has no second implementation to diff Letflow's expr.ex against -- the corpus's real remaining value for Letflow is as a REGRESSION/GOLDEN-VALUE suite: each entry's condition_text (CEL surface syntax, e.g. "variables.order_total > 1000") through expr.ex's existing translate_cel_to_expr/1 (also confirmed present, expr.ex ~L194) and then its evaluator, asserting the result equals the corpus's recorded expected_result under the corpus's own context object bound as variables. SCOPE: port all 15 corpus entries into test/fixtures/simulation/differential_corpus.json verbatim (condition_id, condition_text, context, expected_result preserved byte-for-byte; source_definition_id/source_definition_version/source_gateway_node_id are R-Co-internal cross-references with no Letflow equivalent and may be carried as inert metadata, not resolved). Write one ExUnit test (property-style, iterating the corpus, not 15 hand-written individual tests) asserting Letflow.Engine.Expr's condition-evaluation path (translate_cel_to_expr/1 then evaluate, the same two-stage path transition.ex's dispatch_exclusive_gateway/4 uses) returns each entry's expected_result given its context bound as the variables namespace. Any entry whose condition_text uses a CEL feature expr.ex's @unsupported_call_markers deliberately rejects (per expr.ex's own AC11 section -- macros, type-conversion functions, collection functions, `in`, ternary) is a genuinely expected rejection, not a corpus failure -- inspect all 15 entries' condition_text strings against expr.ex's documented supported grammar (variable refs, 6 comparators, and/or/not, literals, binary arithmetic, unary negation, the 8 REQ-198 builtins) at drafting-adjacent implementation time and record, for any entry outside that grammar, an explicit EXPECTED_UNSUPPORTED disposition with the specific unsupported construct named -- never silently drop the entry from the suite and never force it to "pass" by loosening the assertion. NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no second (CEL) implementation; no change to expr.ex's grammar or supported-builtin set (that is REQ-197/REQ-198's already-closed scope, or a future requirement if a corpus entry reveals a genuine gap -- report such a finding to ORCH rather than silently extending expr.ex here); no business-scenario execution (REQ-206/207/208).
